markdown_report:
**Proposal: coverage-first, budget-matched diagnostic guidance.** At 10% research progress, prioritize establishing whether diagnostics improve model selection before adding elaborate perturbations.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Earlier runs recorded missing panels in all four datasets. Empty perturbation results therefore establish missing execution, not history insensitivity. (2) Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl have substantially higher training-pair ordering errors. This motivates investigating competing candidates, but does not establish worse validation HR@10. (3) Sampled effective-rank fractions near 0.99 provide no obvious evidence of broad collapse. Representation regularization consequently has weaker support than testing ranking and history-use interventions.

**Insights from related work.** (1) DeepMutation motivates checking diagnostics against verified faults and intact controls [1]. Such calibration measures fault detection, not recommendation improvement. (2) Sampled metrics can change model ordering relative to full-catalog evaluation [2]. Training margins and full-catalog sensitivity must therefore remain separate from the pinned selection objective. (3) SASRec reports dataset-dependent positional-ablation effects [3]. A diagnostic direction should generate a testable intervention rather than prescribe universal recency strengthening.

**Framework and directions.** Organize research into execution coverage, calibrated measurement, and prospective intervention selection:

| Layer | Evidence | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage | Valid routes, histories, recommendations | Did diagnosis execute? |
| Calibration | Identity, permutation, verified mutations | Does the probe detect intended faults? |
| Ranking | Uniform versus hard-negative ordering | Which competitors remain unresolved? |
| Selection | Budget-matched validation trials | Does guidance improve search outcomes? |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coverage and mutation calibration [1] | 4/7/4 | Auditable integration; reusable; bounded implementation | Established testing principles; indirect accuracy benefit; architecture hooks required |
| Hard-pool rank audit [2] | 4/7/4 | Focused competitor analysis; actionable; reuses scoring | Familiar sampling analysis; uncertain transfer; sparse transitions |
| Budget-matched guidance experiment [3] | 5/8/5 | Tests diagnostic value; broadly reusable; small intervention menu | Limited algorithmic novelty; noisy validation; requires careful accounting |

**Selected algorithm.** Compare diagnostic guidance, unguided selection, and shuffled guidance using the same SASRec intervention menu: unchanged model, gated recent-history residual, and a fixed harder-negative mixture. Define guidance thresholds and action mappings before observing new outcomes. Randomize menu order for unguided selection; shuffle category-level diagnostic recommendations for the placebo arm.

Give arms equal total GPU budgets, counting diagnostics, failures, and training. Repair panel routing first: use supplied users or deterministically select and record five actual training users/category when none are supplied. Produce unseen full-catalog recommendations for all twenty. Select exclusively by unchanged host macro validation HR@10. A single search comparison remains exploratory; repeated independent search allocations are needed to assess guidance reliability. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Test whether coverage-verified, predefined diagnostic guidance improves validation-selected SASRec interventions compared with unguided and shuffled guidance under equal total GPU budgets.
idea.motivation: Previous diagnostic runs omitted the required user panels, while training-only ranking errors differed across datasets without evidence of broad embedding collapse. The immediate research gap is whether valid diagnostics help choose useful changes, rather than whether increasingly elaborate probes can be constructed.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model as the trained module and adapt item_emb, log2feats and predict_score consistently. Resolve all four dataset routes explicitly. Use supplied panel users when available; otherwise choose five eligible real training users per category with a deterministic local generator, record their IDs, and reuse the panel across arms. Report inability to complete coverage as a failure, never zero sensitivity. Score the full catalog excluding each user's complete original training history, using chunks and deterministic diagnostic tie handling. Preserve module flags and RNG states and avoid consuming the live training iterator. Use only training histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; treat ownership, compatibility, utility and simulator traits as unobserved unless explicit permitted evidence exists. Freeze a common intervention menu and configuration grid before new outcomes: baseline SASRec, a causal recent-history residual with a learned sigmoid gate, and baseline architecture with a fixed mixture of uniform and training-transition negatives. Calibrate diagnostic thresholds using identity controls and verified bounded mutations, without validation-based threshold tuning. Predeclare the mapping from diagnostic patterns to menu order and record abstention when unsupported. All arms use identical training configurations, stopping rules and host validation opportunities; guidance changes ordering only. Partition the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget equally among arms, charge diagnostic and failed-trial costs, and cap diagnostic spending beforehand. Preserve original splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42, all four routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution and the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Update the predictor writer for every architecture or inference change. Host macro validation HR@10 alone selects checkpoints; no test access or claimed benchmark gains.
idea.pseudocode:
freeze intervention_menu, configuration_grid, diagnostic_rules, stopping_rules
split remaining shared GPU budget equally across three arms
for arm in [diagnostic_guidance, unguided, shuffled_guidance]:
    initialize arm ledger
    if arm uses diagnostics:
        for dataset in the four fixed routes:
            resolve and record five actual training panel users
            report = DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)
            require full-catalog unseen-item recommendation coverage
            charge diagnostic cost
        priorities = predefined_rule(report)
        if arm == shuffled_guidance:
            priorities = seeded_permutation_of_category_guidance(priorities)
    else:
        priorities = seeded_random_order(common_intervention_menu)
    while a complete next trial fits the arm budget:
        train next configuration with fixed seeds and original splits
        write matching predictor architecture and checkpoint loading code
        obtain unchanged host macro validation HR@10
        charge all training, debugging and failure costs
        record result without changing diagnostic rules
    retain highest host macro validation HR@10 within arm
report arm outcomes, per-category HR@10, completed trials, coverage and cost
label a single budget allocation exploratory; reserve hidden tests for host final evaluation

originality.positive: Directly tests the incremental value of diagnostic guidance using a common intervention menu, shuffled guidance and explicit search-cost accounting.
originality.negative: Budget-matched comparisons, placebo guidance and gated recency mechanisms are established experimental components; novelty lies mainly in their integration.

future_potential.positive: Can establish whether further diagnostic development is worthwhile and provide a reusable protocol for evaluating recommendation search agents.
future_potential.negative: A small validation panel, adaptive selection and limited repeated search allocations may leave guidance effects uncertain.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses SASRec, existing adapter hooks and a small fixed intervention menu, keeping early implementation manageable.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable dataset routing, panel coverage, accounting, calibrated rules and synchronized predictor generation require careful integration.

related_work.title: DeepMutation: Mutation Testing of Deep Learning Systems
contributions: Provides a mutation-testing precedent for calibrating diagnostics against deliberately altered models.
limitations: Does not establish SASRec-specific diagnostic validity or improvements in recommendation accuracy.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not invalidate the task's pinned sampled-candidate objective; that objective remains the required selection metric.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces SASRec and supplies the task's starting model family.
Reports dataset-dependent effects of architectural ablations, supporting empirical intervention testing.
limitations: Does not establish that stronger recency weighting improves these four datasets or that diagnostic guidance improves search.
